# .github/hex-audit-baseline.txt — the RECORDED advisory set the second CVE
# oracle (scripts/hex-audit-oracle.sh, `mix hex.audit`) already knows about.
#
# WHY IT EXISTS. api/mix.lock and cloud/mix.lock ALREADY carry these advisories
# today, several with no upstream fix (esaml, cowlib, bandit). A rule of "any
# HIGH reds" would therefore red on the untouched, clean lock every single run
# — a gate red before anyone touches it teaches people to ignore it, and it
# could never show the one thing cch-w12-bl-cve-gate-is-oracle-blind criterion
# 2 asks for: clean lock green, hand-reverted lock red.
#
# HOW IT READS. One record per line: `<lock>:<advisory-id>` in field 1; the
# rest of the line is human commentary. `#` starts a comment.
#   an id NOT in this file      -> NEW, the oracle exits 1 (the red that means something)
#   a file id NOT reported      -> CLEARED, printed as a notice, exit stays 0
# A ratchet has two failure directions. This one refuses to red when the world
# got BETTER; it prints the cleared ids and asks you to trim them.
#
# KEYED BY LOCK, NOT BARE. bandit's two HIGHs sit in BOTH locks; a bare-id
# baseline would let an advisory already recorded against api/ arrive in cloud/
# and never read as NEW.
#
# DERIVATION. `bash scripts/hex-audit-oracle.sh`, run 2026-09-09 against
# origin/main 851021379 on Elixir 1.19.5 / OTP 27 (local). 30 records: api 17
# (4 HIGH), cloud 13 (4 HIGH). Regenerate the same way; never hand-add an id
# without saying which run produced it.
